explanation: The N88S mutation reduces atazanavir binding through an indirect conformational mechanism rather than direct ligand contact. Asparagine-to-serine substitution at position 88 removes a larger, polar side chain and decreases local hydrophobicity in the C-terminal dimer region, which destabilizes the structural scaffold supporting the active site geometry at ~7–15 Å distance. This loss of conformational stability likely causes subtle repositioning of downstream residues or altered domain dynamics that propagates to weaken atazanavir's binding mode, even though the mutation itself does not directly contact the inhibitor.
